correctness.rationale: The F mex recurrence follows exactly from chosen maximal chain heads and singleton deletion. The induction on 2a+b proves high-branch 2a+b and low-branch triangular residue values by explicit exhaustive move-value coverage and exclusion. The H recurrence partitions centre-deleting and centre-preserving moves and gives H(a,b)=a for b>=1; its remaining high F options from H(n,0) range from n through 2n-kappa(n), proving the claimed mex. A standalone exact game-graph verifier independently matched labelled star-incidence positions of sizes n=1..8, plus 961 two-level states and 420 centre residuals. No proof step extrapolates finite experiments.

value.rationale: The exact Grundy number, unlike outcome, governs arbitrary disjunctive sums. Star incidence posets grow in both size and width, and the triangular-periodic transition cannot be read off from ordinary parity or a bounded enumeration. The auxiliary two-parameter normal form is naturally forced by maximal-element deletion; it also solves a variable-number-of-piles special case of slow Moore Nim. The theorem is a motivated all-order classification with a nontrivial structural induction, not a routine textbook deduction or isolated small instance.
